profile.headline: Staff Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Objective: A staff software engineering position developing novel software that meets a real need, with a team of hard-working engineers who enjoy working together. An ideal situation would include mentoring of younger engineers, agile software development, and a team with a passion for beautiful code.

Shameless Plug:
"Every day that I spent pair programming with Eric, I would learn something new and valuable."
--Jim Hugunin
--AspectJ: language co-designer; chief architect, compiler & tools
--JPython/Jython, creator

Specialties: -Understanding, employing, adapting complex algorithms.
-Creating, at need, high-performance software with high conceptual integrity.
-Agile software development practices, especially test-driven development and strong refactoring skills to produce elegant, minimalist software.
-Mentoring and informal teaching.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
Creating fast and novel means to detect, isolate, and mitigate software or test errors.

Technical lead for Google's in-house, turn-key continuous integration system.

https://youtu.be/KH2_sB1A6lA

positions.title: Agile Consultant
positions.description: Helping organizations adopt agile software development by working alongside them and getting products out the door.

positions.title: Researcher: The PlayOn Project
positions.description: The PlayOn project (http://blogs.parc.com/playon) is conducting the largest quantitative study of massively multiplayer online role-playing games to date, amassing 190 million sightings of more than 150,000 unique characters, and then analyzed this data to better understand the social dynamics of these artificial worlds. My role on this project has been to facilitate the trade-off the team has had to take between understanding what data can be harvested from the MMO, and what analyses it can be used for, as well as the design and construction of the embedded "bot" software which collects this data. As part of the team's "hive mind", I have suggested many of the analyses carried out by the team's sociologists.

positions.title: Researcher: Improving Software Development
positions.description: The work centered around 3 separate projects: (1) Working with a Jim Hugunin-led team to do complex static and dynamic analysis of extremely large code bases; (2) initiated project to utilize agile test suites to automatically suggest software improvements; (3) joined bi-cultural ethnographic team studying means to improve software development in gigantic Asian firm, functioning as knowledgable practictioner and agile evangelist.

positions.title: Researcher: High-Performance Java Imager
positions.description: Ported the high-performance Parc Cedar Imager to Java. The original Imager was written in the proprietary Cedar language, and is at the heart of Xerox' Docuprint line of high-speed printers. As well as re-architecting for languages, and removing optimizations that were no longer necessary, I produced a comprehensive agilen test suite, and a pdf decomposer able to drive the Java Imager.

positions.title: Research Software Developer
positions.description: Developed software for novel imaging technologies. During 1990s position was part-time (except 18 months ca 1994).

positions.title: Cross-Cultural Bridge Builder
positions.description: Lived in remote corners of Asia for the purpose of building social ties that led to constructive religious dialog between people of widely different backgrounds. An significant portion of this work involved extensive language and culture learning, including 2.5 years living in a village without electricity or running water.

positions.title: Game Designer
positions.description: Designed two unreleased games for Atari 400/800 home computers, as well as a rewrite of Tom Loughry's "The Dreadnaught Factor" (originally on the Mattel Intellivision) for the Atari 400/800 home computers.

positions.title: Software developer
positions.description: Team lead for implementation of BASIC interpreter for computer console add-on to Mattel's Intellivision which was never released.
